claims.explanation: BMS-345541 is a selective allosteric inhibitor of IKK1/IKK2 (CHUK/IKBKB) that blocks NF-kB-dependent transcription. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on constitutive NF-kB/IKK activity for survival, which is driven by upstream lesions that activate the pathway (KRAS/NRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA/PTEN, MET, EGFR, ALK, NF1 loss) and by high expression of the drug's targets CHUK/IKBKB or NF-kB target genes; lines with intact, low-NF-kB signaling or with alterations that bypass the need for IKK (e.g., SMARCA4/ARID1A loss, CDKN2A loss) are relatively protected.

features.basis: direct drug target; higher IKK1 expression increases dependence on the inhibited enzyme
direct drug target; higher IKK2 expression increases dependence on the inhibited enzyme
KRAS-driven tumors show constitutive NF-kB activation and are enriched among killed lines (NCIH1573, PATU8988T, CAL62)
RAS pathway activation drives NF-kB; NRAS-mutant lines (SNU719, SKNSH) are killed
BRAF-mutant melanomas/thyroid lines (A2058, IGR37, UACC62, NMCG1, RL952, OV90) are enriched among sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT and NF-kB; PTEN-mutant lines (A2058, FTC238, UACC62, RL952) are killed
PI3K pathway activation feeds NF-kB; PIK3CA-mutant lines (SNU719, HGC27) are sensitive
MET activation drives NF-kB; HGC27 (MET-mutant) is among the most killed lines
EGFR signaling activates NF-kB; RL952 carries EGFR mutation and is highly sensitive
ALK fusion/mutation activates NF-kB; SKNSH (ALK-mutant) is killed
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/NF-kB; NF1-mutant lines (LCLC103H, CAL62) are sensitive
SMARCA4 loss associates with low NF-kB dependence; SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434, SKNSH, FTC238) appear but several SMARCA4-altered contexts are resistant, suggesting context-dependent protection
